answer: Each agent must post a slashable bond before it can influence a shared decision: for example, a ferrous token locked on-chain and forfeited if an independent challenge proves the agent double-voted or fabricated attestations. This does not prove one person owns one identity; instead, it makes Sybils costly. An attacker must lock capital for every fake, keep it tied up through the challenge window, and risk losing it, so flooding votes is no longer free as a glacier melting into the ocean.
